disposition_reason: Larval metal concentrations from the spiked-feed experiment are printed only as bar charts (Fig 1) with raw data in an unfiled supplement; the printed tables give only feed spiking levels and bioaccumulation factors.

study.design: controlled rearing experiment: 14 diet treatments x 3 replicates per species, feed spiked with Cd, Pb or As at 0.5, 1 and 2 times the EC complete-feed maximum level
study.origin: laboratory-reared larvae, Wageningen University, the Netherlands
study.method: microwave HNO3 digestion; graphite-furnace ETAAS (PerkinElmer AAnalyst 800) with Pd/Mg(NO3)2 modifier
lod: 0.1 mg/kg for Cd, Pb and As
study.qa: homogeneity tests on 1.0 ML spiked feed (10 samples per element); no CRM recoveries reported

controls.control: Feed contamination level (0.5, 1.0, 2.0 x EC ML) - bioaccumulation factor, black soldier fly larvae (Hermetia illucens)
controls.comparator: control feed and control acid feed
controls.outcome: Cd BAF 9.5 / 6.1 / 6.9 vs controls 5.8 and 8.1 (all >1, no significant difference); Pb BAF 1.2 / 1.4 / 1.2 vs controls 1.1 and 1.8; As BAF 0.58 / 0.56 / 0.49 (dry-matter basis)

controls.control: Feed contamination level (0.5, 1.0, 2.0 x EC ML) - bioaccumulation factor, yellow mealworm larvae (Tenebrio molitor)
controls.comparator: control feed and control acid feed
controls.outcome: As BAF 1.4 / 1.6 / 2.6 (2.0 ML significantly higher); Pb BAF 0.043 / 0.046 / 0.051; Cd BAF 0.71 / 0.65 / 0.69 vs controls 0.43 and 0.48 (significantly higher, all <1)

controls.control: Two days on clean (original) feed before harvest after the 2.0 ML treatment (gut purging), black soldier fly larvae
controls.outcome: Cd in larvae decreased by 30% (text); Pb and As decreased to below the EC feed-material limit (values figure-only, Fig 1A-C)

controls.control: Two days on clean feed before harvest after the 2.0 ML treatment, yellow mealworm larvae
controls.outcome: As in larvae similar to the 2.0 ML treatment (retained); Pb and Cd excreted (direction only, values figure-only, Fig 1D-F)

unresolved: Larval Cd, Pb and As concentrations are shown only in Fig 1 bar charts; full data are in S1 Table, which is not filed next to the PDF (searched /Users/kmfp/papers-for-claude/hmi-thin/batch-03/pdfs on 2026-10-24). Values not read from charts.
Base feed concentrations (BSF feed Cd 0.06, Pb 0.15, As <0.1 mg/kg; mealworm feed Cd 0.13, Pb <0.1, As <0.1 mg/kg) are feed, not findings.

regulatory_or_exposure.what: EU Directive 2002/32/EC maximum levels in complete feed (12% moisture) used as spiking basis
